page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd5 is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 9255 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with dedicated allocation, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, which equates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a local 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several areas. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and single-threaded compression tasks rank in the top 10%. Memory subsystem performance is also notable, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% and read-only memory bandwidth reaching 5282.07 GB/sec for small cached blocks. Multi-core performance, including the Passmark CPU score and stress-ng multi-core metrics, falls within the top 25%. However, large-block memory write bandwidth is moderate, placing in the middle 50% at 88.06 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and web serving. The server achieves top-tier throughput for static web serving at 102.69 GB/sec and strong database performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 84.77 million operations per second. It also supports small-scale machine learning tasks, demonstrating top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for 135M parameter models, though performance drops to average levels for prompt processing on 7B models. The bare metal architecture offers high resource density and dedicated compute power, providing qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring sustained CPU and memory utilization without virtualization overhead.
